extracted.intended_audience: State Departments of Transportation (State DOTs), Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), and other transportation planners and stakeholders affected by FHWA performance management rules
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule and preamble establishing a Greenhouse Gas (GHG) performance measure for the National Highway System (NHS), specifying the metric and measure definitions, target-setting and reporting requirements, data sources and calculation conventions, deadlines, and significant-progress determinations for State DOTs and MPOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA authority scope for the measure
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA's authority to apply this measure is limited to the Interstate System and the non-Interstate National Highway System (NHS) under 23 U.S.C. 150(c)(3)(A)(ii)(IV)-(V).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency notes it only has authority to apply this measure to the Interstate System and the non-Interstate NHS; it does not claim unlimited authority beyond those systems. (Preamble discussion citing 23 U.S.C. 150(c)(3)(A)(ii)(IV)-(V)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish declining targets
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs and MPOs are required to establish declining targets for greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions on the NHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA requires declining targets for CO2 emissions but is not setting specific target values nor mandating penalties for failing to achieve targets. Targets should indicate a reduction in CO2 emissions. (See discussion and 23 CFR 490.105(e)(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA not prescribing specific targets or penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA is neither requiring any specific targets nor mandating any penalties for failing to achieve these targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and MPOs set and determine targets based on appropriate data, policies, and priorities; FHWA will not prescribe what declining targets look like in each State or MPO. (Preamble statements; consistent with 23 U.S.C. 145 state project financing authorities.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'performance' to include environmental performance
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA interprets 'performance' of the Interstate System and non-Interstate NHS under 23 U.S.C. 150(c)(3)(A)(ii)(IV)-(V) to include environmental performance, including greenhouse gas emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation is informed by the statutory national goals (including environmental sustainability at 23 U.S.C. 150(b)(6)), related Title 23 provisions, and the risks climate change poses to NHS condition and performance; it supports establishing a GHG measure under FHWA's TPM authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG measure definition (percent change)
rubrics_metrics.description: The finalized GHG measure is the percent change in tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS relative to the reference year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA selected this measure for sensitivity to transportation policies, simplicity, ease of calculation, and reliance on data States already report to FHWA. The measure is calculated using the GHG metric (CO2 in mmt) for the current year and the reference year. (Preamble and 23 CFR references, e.g., 23 CFR 490.513(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG metric definition (absolute emissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHG metric is defined as the calculation of tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS for a given year computed in million metric tons (mmt) and rounded to the nearest hundredth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State DOTs calculate the metric per 23 CFR 490.511(c); the metric is the basis for computing the percent-change measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference year selection
rubrics_metrics.description: 2022 is established as the reference year for the GHG measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA changed the definition in 23 CFR 490.505 and updated the calculation in 23 CFR 490.513(d) accordingly. The HPMS data as of November 30, 2023, will be used to calculate the metric for the reference year. (Preamble VI.A, VI.D.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Net-zero language removal
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'net-zero' was removed from 23 CFR 490.101, and targets are not required to demonstrate reductions toward net-zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 490.105(e)(10) was revised so targets must be declining for reducing tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS, but they are not required to demonstrate reductions toward net-zero targets. (Preamble VI.B.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial target timeframe (4-year targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial targets to be established are 4-year targets; 2-year targets will not be established for the initial cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the initial 4-year target, the reference year will be used as the baseline. (23 CFR 490.105(e)(1), 490.105(e)(4)(iii), 490.105(e)(10)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance period dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The performance period for the GHG measure begins January 1, 2022 and extends 4 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This performance period establishes the timeframe for the initial target and reporting cycles. (23 CFR 490.105(e)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Initial GHG Report content and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs must submit a State Initial GHG Report by February 1, 2024, including the State DOT's 4-year target for the GHG measure, the basis for the target, a discussion of how the target relates to other longer-term performance expectations, and the metric information for the reference year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting requirement is in 23 CFR 490.107(d). Because of the 2024 Initial Report, States will not include additional GHG information in the 2024 Mid Performance Period Progress Report. Metric reported will be calculated using the data specified in 23 CFR 490.107(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biennial reporting start and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Biennial reporting related to the GHG measure begins with the 2026 Full Performance Period Progress Report; 2- and 4-year targets will be reported in the 2026 Baseline Performance Period Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA revised 23 CFR 490.107(b)(1)-(3) accordingly; biennial reporting cycles thereafter follow the TPM rules as revised in this final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant progress determination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 2026 Full Performance Period Progress Report, FHWA will determine whether a State DOT has made significant progress toward the achievement of the 4-year target for the GHG measure, using specified data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA will use the data described in 23 CFR 490.109(d)(1) when calculating actual performance and making significant progress determinations. The performance for the reference year will be used as the baseline for the 2026 significant progress determination. Significant progress determination requirements for the GHG measure will be phased in as described in 23 CFR 490.109(e)(6). FHWA will not determine significant progress toward 2-year targets in 2024 because 2-year targets are not established initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: State DOT vs MPO calculation roles
rubrics_metrics.description: 23 CFR 490.511 includes different requirements for State DOTs and MPOs when calculating the metric: the State DOT's method is defined and uniform across states; MPOs are granted flexibility in how they calculate the metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State DOT method: 23 CFR 490.511(c) (same for all states). MPO method: 23 CFR 490.511(d) grants flexibility; final rule removed proposed requirement for mutual agreement on method and instead requires MPOs to report their method and, if using a non-specified method, to demonstrate the method produces valid and useful results (23 CFR 490.107(c)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO metric-method reporting and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs must report a description of their metric calculation method(s); when the method is not one specified in 23 CFR 490.511(d), the MPO must include information demonstrating the method(s) has valid and useful results for measuring transportation-related CO2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the proposed requirement for MPOs and State DOTs to mutually agree on a method; MPOs must document and justify alternative methods in biennial reports. (23 CFR 490.107(c)(2)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data inputs and source definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate the metric, State DOTs require several data inputs defined in 23 CFR 490.511(c); the data requirements are defined in 23 CFR 490.509; FHWA defines the specific data sources it will use when it calculates the metric and measure for significant progress determinations in 23 CFR 490.109(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule clarifies which data are required, how they are to be used, and what FHWA will rely upon for official calculations used in significant progress determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: VMT data use and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs may use their best available vehicle miles traveled (VMT) data when establishing targets, reporting baseline and actual performance, and discussing progress; the VMT data should represent the prior calendar year and be consistent with final HPMS submissions to the maximum extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision addresses timing concerns about HPMS finalization. For FHWA calculations for significant progress determinations, FHWA will use HPMS data available on November 30 of the determination year (for reference year, HPMS as of Nov 30, 2023). (See 23 CFR 490.509(h) and 490.109(d)(1)(vi)-(vii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: State biennial reporting of metric components and VMT data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs must report the GHG metric value they calculated, the individual values used to calculate the GHG metric, and a description of the data source(s) used for the VMT information in biennial reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule removed the proposed requirement to report CO2 emissions on all public roads because values used to calculate the NHS GHG metric can be used to calculate all-roads values; reporting must include underlying components and VMT data source descriptions to ensure transparency and comparability. (Revisions to proposed 23 CFR 490.107 reporting provisions and 23 CFR 490.511(f)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CO2 factors specified in regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The significant progress determination will use the CO2 factors specified in 23 CFR 490.509(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 490.109(d)(1)(viii) specifies that FHWA will apply the CO2 factors in 490.509(f) for calculation consistency in significant progress determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA calculation data cutoff for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For significant progress and baseline/actual performance calculations, FHWA will use HPMS data available on November 30 of the year the significant progress determination is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a uniform data cutoff for FHWA's internal calculations (for reference year, HPMS as of Nov 30, 2023). See 23 CFR 490.109(d)(1)(vi)-(vii).
